title: Nanoscale magnetometry via collective many-body dynamics in diamond
authors: Haoyang Gao, Piotr Put, Nathaniel T. Leitao, Nazlı U. Köylüoğlu, Andrew Maccabe, Mathew Mammen, Siddharth Dandavate, Lillian B. Hughes Wyatt, Leigh S. Martin, Ania C. Bleszynski Jayich, Hongkun Park, Mikhail D. Lukin
abstract: Many-body dynamics constitutes a promising approach for creating correlations between quantum particles which can be used for applications in sensing and metrology. However, utilizing this potential for substantial gains in practical settings is a challenging task with only a very few applications realized to date. Here, we demonstrate an approach to nanoscale magnetic sensing enabled by strongly interacting electronic spins in a room temperature solid. By coherently controlling collective many-body dynamics of a dipolar ensemble of $\sim 10^4$ nitrogen-vacancy (NV) centres in diamond with pulsed magnetic field gradients, we demonstrate practical metrological gain up to $7.9(2)\,\mathrm{dB}$ for magnetic signal detection and $8.8(3)\,\mathrm{dB}$ for magnetic noise sensing, fully accounting for experimental overheads. Finally, we combine these methods to demonstrate a momentum-space-resolved sensing modality that enables detection of spatially correlated magnetic noise at continuously tunable length scales down to 50 nanometers. These observations open the door toward practical applications of interaction-enhanced quantum sensors for nanoscale biological imaging and material characterization.
summary: This work presents a novel approach to nanoscale magnetometry using strongly interacting electron spins in diamond NV centers. By coherently controlling collective many-body dynamics via Overhauser-Antiferromagnetic Tunneling (OAT), the authors achieve significant signal amplification and demonstrate the ability to map spatially correlated magnetic noise down to 50 nm. This opens pathways for advanced quantum sensing in biological and material characterization.
main_problem: The paper addresses the challenge of achieving practical, high-gain nanoscale magnetic sensing by leveraging the collective many-body dynamics of interacting quantum spins.
main_result: They successfully demonstrate metrological gains up to 8.8 dB for noise sensing and achieve momentum-space-resolved detection of spatially correlated magnetic noise down to 50 nm.
method: The core method involves engineering Overhauser-Antiferromagnetic Tunneling (OAT) dynamics using pulsed magnetic field gradients to coherently control and amplify the sensing signal.
model_or_system: The system is a high-density ensemble of Nitrogen-Vacancy (NV) centers in diamond, whose dynamics are governed by magnetic dipole-dipole interactions, modeled via collective spin-wave dynamics.
key_observables: Metrological gain (dB), spatial resolution (nm), spin polarization dynamics, and the response function $F(\vec{k}_n, \vec{K})$.
important_parameters: The sensing gain (e.g., 7.9 dB for signal, 8.8 dB for noise), the minimum detectable length scale (50 nm), and the interaction strength parameter $J_0$.
main_assumptions: The analysis accounts for experimental overheads, and theoretical derivations rely on mean-field approximations and specific symmetries in the spin-wave model.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the experimental setup, the multi-stage signal amplification protocol (OAT), and the theoretical prediction of momentum-space response functions $F(\vec{k}_n, \vec{K})$ showing wavevector selectivity.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from demonstrating the physical system and the need for interaction enhancement, detailing the OAT protocol for signal amplification, and culminating in a theoretical analysis of the momentum-space response function to characterize spatially correlated noise.
why_interesting: The use of collective dynamics and engineered spin interactions in a solid-state platform like NV centers provides a concrete, experimentally realized example of how many-body physics can enhance quantum sensing beyond the standard quantum limit.
